assertions.text: The response delivers a complete test file. Open questions may be noted as assumptions alongside the delivered tests, but the response must not stop at clarifying questions instead of delivering.
assertions.evidence: Full test file with 12 parametrized cases delivered, no clarifying questions asked.

assertions.text: The ambiguity in the rules (how the 20-euro cap interacts with the children's half rate) is resolved to an explicit, stated interpretation — in the response text, a comment, or scenario ids — not silently embedded in expected values.
assertions.evidence: # The 20-euro cap (2000 cents) is a flat ceiling ... the children's discount does not also apply to the cap itself.

assertions.text: Cases cover the interaction between the cap and the children's half rate: a children's-section book late enough to reach the cap appears with a concrete expected fee — not just each rule tested in isolation.
assertions.evidence: pytest.param(80, True, 2000, id="at the cap boundary, children's section")

assertions.text: Cases include zero days late (no fee), an ordinary per-day fee, and a return late enough to hit the cap for a regular book — the rule set's boundaries, not just one happy-path row.
Tests use @pytest.mark.parametrize (or pytest.param rows) — not one test function per case, and not a loop over cases inside a single test body.
Parametrized cases carry scenario identifiers — an ids= argument or pytest.param(..., id=...) — so each case has a readable name in test output.
assertions.evidence: Parametrized cases carry ids (ids= or pytest.param id=)

assertions.text: Test function bodies contain no if/elif statements — expected outcomes come from the parametrized data, not branching logic.
assertions.evidence: No if/elif statements in test function bodies

assertions.text: Expected fees are concrete cent values (e.g. 150, 2000) readable directly from the cases — not computed inside the test body from the rate and days.
assertions.evidence: pytest.param(10, False, 500, id="ten days late, standard section")

assertions.text: pytest can import and collect the test modules against the project scaffolding
